# Data Wrangling

```{r data wrangling, include = T}
#branch clipping sample data
lep_biomass_2025 <- read.csv("lep_biomass_2025.csv",
                             stringsAsFactors = T)

#vegetation survey data
veg_data_2025 <- read.csv("veg_data_2025.csv",
                          stringsAsFactors = T)

#output from iTree
itree_data <- read.csv("itree_output_height.csv",
                         stringsAsFactors = T)

#create property variable
lep_biomass_2025$property <- substr(lep_biomass_2025$vegpoint, 1, 3)

## CATERPILLAR ABUNDANCE DATA

#combining the number of caterpillars per sample regardless of size or palatability category
lep_biomass_2025 <- mutate(lep_biomass_2025,
                            total_cat = sm_smooth_cat + 
                            med_smooth_cat +
                            lg_smooth_cat + 
                            small_hairy_cat +
                            med_hairy_cat +
                            lg_hairy_cat)

## CATERPILLAR BIOMASS DATA

#combining dry biomass of smooth and hairy categories
lep_biomass_2025 <- mutate(lep_biomass_2025,
                           cat_g = 
                             smooth_cat_dry_mass_g +
                             hairy_cat_dry_mass_g)

#dry caterpillar biomass / dry leaf biomass
lep_biomass_2025 <- mutate(lep_biomass_2025,
                           cat_branch = 
                             cat_g/tree_dry_mass_g)

#merging caterpillar and iTree data
lep_biomass_2025 <- merge(lep_biomass_2025, itree_data,
                           by = c("plot_ID", "tree_species",
                                  "tree_height_m"))

#filtering out trees with a DBH smaller than 10
lep_biomass_2025 <- lep_biomass_2025 %>% filter(dbh_cm.x >= 10)

#converting dry leaf biomass of entire tree from kg to g
lep_biomass_2025 <- mutate(lep_biomass_2025,
                           leaf_biomass_g = leaf_biomass_kg * 1000)

#multiplying caterpillar/branch biomass (g) by leaf biomass of entire tree (g)
lep_biomass_2025$cat_tree <- lep_biomass_2025$cat_branch * lep_biomass_2025$leaf_biomass_g

## VEGETATION DATA

#removing observations with no veg surveys
lep_biomass_2025 <- lep_biomass_2025 %>% filter(veg_survey != "no")

#combining large and small shrubs, multiplying small by 0.5 to weight by differences in shrub biomass
veg_data_2025$blackberry <- veg_data_2025$lg_blackberry +
  veg_data_2025$sm_blackberry * 0.5

veg_data_2025$coralberry <- veg_data_2025$lg_coralberry +
  veg_data_2025$sm_coralberry * 0.5

veg_data_2025$olive <- veg_data_2025$lg_olive + 
  veg_data_2025$sm_olive * 0.5

veg_data_2025$mfr <- veg_data_2025$lg_mfr +
  veg_data_2025$sm_mfr * 0.5

veg_data_2025$barberry <- veg_data_2025$lg_barberry +
  veg_data_2025$sm_barberry * 0.5

veg_data_2025$honeysuckle <- veg_data_2025$lg_honeysuckle +
  veg_data_2025$sm_honeysuckle * 0.5

veg_data_2025$other_nativeShrub <- veg_data_2025$lg_other_nativeShrub +
  veg_data_2025$sm_other_nativeShrub * 0.5

veg_data_2025$other_nonnativeShrub <- veg_data_2025$lg_other_nonnativeShrub +
  veg_data_2025$sm_other_nonnativeShrub * 0.5

#including trees in veg neighborhood
veg_data_2025 <- veg_data_2025 %>% 
  mutate(all_trees = sm_locust + med_locust + lg_locust + 
           sm_maple + med_maple + lg_maple +
           sm_oak + med_oak + lg_oak +
           sm_cherry + med_cherry + lg_cherry +
           sm_apple + med_apple + lg_apple + 
           sm_ash + med_ash + lg_ash + 
           sm_hickory + med_hickory + lg_hickory + 
           sm_walnut + med_walnut + lg_walnut +
           sm_hawthorn + med_hawthorn + lg_hawthorn +
           sm_elm + med_elm + lg_elm + 
           sm_birch + med_birch + lg_birch +
           sm_othertree + med_othertree + lg_othertree)

#including both first and second distance bands weighted equally
veg_data_2025 <- veg_data_2025 %>% filter(distance_tree != "1")

#making proportion native column including shrubs, saplings, and vines
veg_data_2025 <- veg_data_2025 %>% 
  mutate(native_veg = blackberry + other_nativeShrub +
           all_trees + grape + creeper + clematis + other_nativeVine) %>% 
  mutate(nonnative_veg = olive + barberry + mfr + coralberry + 
           honeysuckle + other_nonnativeShrub + obittersweet) %>% 
  mutate(totalveg = native_veg + nonnative_veg,
         prop_native = native_veg/totalveg)

#making this number a percentage by dividing by the max value and multiplying by 100
veg_data_2025$totalveg <- (veg_data_2025$totalveg/312.5) * 100

#merging caterpillar, tree, and vegetation data
lep_biomass_2025 <- left_join(lep_biomass_2025, veg_data_2025,
                      by = c("plot_ID", "tree_species", 
                             "vegpoint", "letter_code"))

#dropping redundant columns
lep_biomass_2025 <- subset(lep_biomass_2025, 
                                select = -c(date.x, date.y))

## VEGETATION DIVERSITY
#combining all tree size classes for diversity
lep_biomass_2025 <- lep_biomass_2025 %>% 
  mutate(locust = sm_locust + med_locust + lg_locust,
         maple = sm_maple + med_maple + lg_maple,
         oak = sm_oak + med_oak + lg_oak,
         cherry = sm_cherry + med_cherry + lg_cherry,
         apple = sm_apple + med_apple + lg_apple,
         ash = sm_ash + med_ash + lg_ash,
         hickory = sm_hickory + med_hickory + lg_hickory,
         walnut = sm_walnut + med_walnut + lg_walnut,
         hawthorn = sm_hawthorn + med_hawthorn + lg_hawthorn,
         elm = sm_elm + med_elm + lg_elm,
         birch = sm_birch + med_birch + lg_birch,
         othertree = sm_othertree + med_othertree + lg_othertree)

#total richness
tot_rich <- select(lep_biomass_2025, blackberry, coralberry,
                 olive, mfr, barberry, honeysuckle, other_nativeShrub,
                 other_nonnativeShrub, locust, maple, oak, cherry,
                 apple, ash, hickory, walnut, hawthorn, elm, birch,
                 othertree, grape, creeper, clematis, othervine,
                 obittersweet)

veg_rich <- rowSums(tot_rich > 0)
lep_biomass_2025$veg_rich <- veg_rich

#native richness
native_rich <- select(lep_biomass_2025, blackberry, other_nativeShrub,
                      locust, maple, oak, cherry, apple, ash, hickory,
                      walnut, hawthorn, elm, birch, othertree, grape,
                      creeper, clematis, othervine)

native_veg_rich <- rowSums(native_rich > 0)
lep_biomass_2025$native_veg_rich <- native_veg_rich

#shannon diversity of all vegetation
shannondiv <- diversity(tot_rich)
lep_biomass_2025$shannondiv <- shannondiv

#shannon diversity of native vegetation
native_shannondiv <- diversity(native_rich)
lep_biomass_2025$native_shannondiv <- native_shannondiv

```

# Abundance GLMMs

```{r total cat abundance glmm}
#selecting model family
#poisson
total_cat_pois <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                  offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                  data = lep_biomass_2025,
                  ziformula = ~0,
                  family = poisson)

#negative binomial 1
total_cat_nbin1 <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,
                   family = nbinom1)

#negative binomial 2
total_cat_nbin2 <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,
                   family = nbinom2)

#zero-truncated negative binomial 2
total_cat_nbin2_zh <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                          offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                          data = lep_biomass_2025,
                          ziformula = ~1,
                          family = truncated_nbinom2)

AICctab(total_cat_pois, total_cat_nbin1, total_cat_nbin2, total_cat_nbin2_zh)

summary(total_cat_nbin2)
check_model(total_cat_nbin2, size_dot = 1.2) 
check_overdispersion(total_cat_nbin2)
check_zeroinflation(total_cat_nbin2)

#zi formula
total_cat_nbin2_z <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~1,
                   family = nbinom2)

total_cat_nbin2_sp <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~tree_species,
                   family = nbinom2)

total_cat_nbin2_pnat <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + 
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~prop_native,
                   family = nbinom2)

AICctab(total_cat_nbin2, total_cat_nbin2_z, 
       total_cat_nbin2_sp, total_cat_nbin2_pnat)

#assess property as random effect
total_cat_nbin2_re <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + (1|property) +
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,
                   family = nbinom2)

AICtab(total_cat_nbin2, total_cat_nbin2_re)

summary(total_cat_nbin2_re)
check_model(total_cat_nbin2_re, size_dot = 1.2) 
check_overdispersion(total_cat_nbin2_re)
check_zeroinflation(total_cat_nbin2_re)

#dispersion parameter
total_cat_nbin2_d <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + (1|property) +
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,
                   dispformula = ~week,
                   family = nbinom2)

AICctab(total_cat_nbin2, total_cat_nbin2_re, total_cat_nbin2_d)

#test hypotheses
total_cat_null <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ 1 + (1|property) +
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,
                   family = nbinom2)

total_cat_spp <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + (1|property) +
                   offset(log(tree_dry_mass_g)),
                   data = lep_biomass_2025,
                   ziformula = ~0,

#additive
total_cat_veg_add <- glmmTMB(total_cat ~ tree_species + totalveg + (1|property) +
```

## Abundance Plots

```{r total cat abundance plot}
#blackberry abundance plot
pred_total_cat_bla_add <- predict_response(total_cat_bla_add,
                         terms = c("blackberry", "tree_species"), 
                         condition = c(tree_dry_mass_g = 1),
                         bias_correction = T)

#adjust raw data to align with predicted
lep_biomass_2025$cat_per_gram <- 
  lep_biomass_2025$total_cat / lep_biomass_2025$tree_dry_mass_g

abund_plot1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = lep_biomass_2025, 
             aes(x = blackberry, y = cat_per_gram,
                 color = tree_species))+
  geom_line(data = pred_total_cat_bla_add, aes(x = x,
                                       y = predicted,
                                       color = group))+
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_total_cat_bla_add,
              aes(x = x,
                  ymin = conf.low,
                  ymax = conf.high,
                  fill = group), alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_text(aes(x = 93, y = 1.4, label = "A", size = 25),
            colour="black")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = 
                      c("tomato2", "slateblue", "forestgreen"))+
  scale_color_manual(values = 
                       c("tomato2", "slateblue", "forestgreen"))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(x = "Blackberry percent cover \nwithin 10 m",
       y = "Predicted caterpillar abundance \nper g dry leaf biomass",
       color = "Tree Species",
       fill = "Tree Species")

#native richness abundance plot
pred_total_cat_natVegRich_add <-
  predict_response(total_cat_natVegRich_add,
                         terms = c("native_veg_rich", "tree_species"), 
                         condition = c(tree_dry_mass_g = 24),
                         bias_correction = T)

abund_plot2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = lep_biomass_2025,
             aes(x = native_veg_rich,
                 y = total_cat,
                 color = tree_species))+
  geom_line(data = pred_total_cat_natVegRich_add,
            aes(x = x,
                y = predicted,
                color = group))+
  geom_ribbon(data = pred_total_cat_natVegRich_add,
              aes(x = x,
                  ymin = conf.low,
                  ymax = conf.high,
                  fill = group), alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_text(aes(x = 9.5, y = 43.8, label = "B", size = 25),
            colour="black")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = 
                      c("tomato2", "slateblue", "forestgreen"))+
  scale_color_manual(values = 
                       c("tomato2", "slateblue", "forestgreen"))+
  theme_bw()+

  theme(legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.75, 0.70),
        legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black"))+

       y = "",
       color = "Tree Species",
       fill = "Tree Species")

grid.arrange(abund_plot1, abund_plot2, nrow = 1)
```

## Abundance Effects Plot

```{r abundance effects plot}
# 1. Complete list of 11 additive models
new_model_list <- list(
  "Veg. Density"      = total_cat_veg_add,
  "Prop. Native"         = total_cat_nat_add, 
  "% Autumn olive"          = total_cat_ao_add, 
  "% Multiflora rose"            = total_cat_mfr_add, 
  "% Barberry"       = total_cat_bar_add, 
  "% Blackberry"     = total_cat_bla_add, 
  "% Coralberry"     = total_cat_cor_add, 
  "Richness"       = total_cat_vegRich_add,
  "Native Richness"     = total_cat_natVegRich_add, 
  "Shannon Div."        = total_cat_shannon_add,
  "Native Shannon Div."  = total_cat_natShannon_add)

# 2. AUTOMATIC AIC EXTRACTION: Grab AICs and find the top models
# We calculate delta AIC (dAIC). Any model within 2 units of the absolute lowest AIC is a "top model"
aic_values <- sapply(new_model_list, AIC)
min_aic <- min(aic_values)

aic_df <- data.frame(
  predictor = names(aic_values),
  aic = aic_values,
  daic = aic_values - min_aic,
  # Dynamically flag if a model is among the best (dAIC <= 2)
  is_best = (aic_values - min_aic) <= 2
)

# 3. Extract standardized parameters and force them into dataframes
standardized_list <- lapply(new_model_list, function(mod) {
  as.data.frame(standardize_parameters(mod, method = "refit", ci = 0.95))
})

all_standardized <- bind_rows(standardized_list, .id = "Predictor")
names(all_standardized) <- tolower(names(all_standardized))

# 4. Exact lowercase terms matching your continuous model predictors
target_terms <- c(
  "totalveg", "prop_native", "olive", "mfr", "barberry", "blackberry", 
  "coralberry", "veg_rich", "native_veg_rich", "shannondiv", "native_shannondiv"
)

# 5. Filter, merge AIC flags, and build conditional formatting
plot_data <- all_standardized %>%
  filter(parameter %in% target_terms) %>%
  left_join(aic_df, by = "predictor") %>%
  mutate(
    # Keep ordering by effect size size, or change to '-aic' if you want top models at the top
    predictor = fct_reorder(predictor, std_coefficient),
    
    # STRATEGY 1: Add asterisks dynamically to the text labels of top models
    text_label = ifelse(is_best,
                        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f) *", std_coefficient, ci_low, ci_high),
                        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", std_coefficient, ci_low, ci_high)),
    
    # Create a nice group variable for ggplot coloring
    highlight_group = ifelse(is_best, "Top Model (dAIC ≤ 2)", "Other Model")
  )

# 6. Define axis boundaries for the standardized variables
x_lower_limit <- -1.5
x_upper_limit <- 1.5

# 7. Generate the final styled forest plot
abund_effects_plot <- 
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(y = predictor, color = highlight_group)) +
  # Baseline zero line (No effect)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Standardized confidence intervals
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), height = 0.15, linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Standardized point estimates
  geom_point(aes(x = std_coefficient), size = 4) +
  
  # STRATEGY 2: Dynamic text table on the right margin 
  # We make the text bold if it is a top model to double down on formatting
  # geom_text(aes(x = x_upper_limit + 0.5, label = text_label, fontface = ifelse(is_best, "bold", "plain")), 
  #           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "black") +
  
  # Set your specific custom colors (e.g., sharp dark red for top models, slate grey for others)
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top Model (dAIC ≤ 2)" = "firebrick3", "Other Model" = "lightsteelblue4")) +
  
  # Prevent extra-wide confidence intervals from ruining the visual layout
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(x_lower_limit, x_upper_limit), clip = "on") +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.2))) + # Reserves 45% empty space on the right
  labs(
    title = "Caterpillar Abundance",
    #subtitle = "Top performing AIC models highlighted in red with an asterisk (*)",
    x = "Standardized Coefficient (95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Model Fit (AIC)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    #legend.position = "bottom" # Puts the color legend cleanly at the bottom
  )+
  geom_text(aes(x = -1.5, y = 11, label = "A"),
            colour="black")
```

```{r total cat bm glmm}
            ziformula=~0,

#zero-inflated gamma model
cat_bm_zigamma <- glmmTMB(cat_tree ~ 1,
            family=ziGamma(link="log"),
            ziformula=~1, #need to use 1; non-positive values not allowed
            data=lep_biomass_2025)

AICctab(cat_bm_tweedie, cat_bm_zigamma)

r2(cat_bm_zigamma)
check_model(cat_bm_zigamma, size_dot = 1.2)

#zi formula
```

# Biomass Effects Plot

```{r biomass effects plot}
# 1. Your complete list of 11 models
bm_model_list <- list(
  "Veg. Density"      = cat_bm_veg,
  "Prop. Native"  = cat_bm_nat, 
  "% Autumn olive"          = cat_bm_ao, 
  "% Multiflora rose"  = cat_bm_mfr, 
  "% Barberry"       = cat_bm_bar, 
  "% Blackberry"     = cat_bm_bla, 
  "% Coralberry"     = cat_bm_cor, 
  "Richness"       = cat_bm_vegRich,
  "Native Richness"     = cat_bm_natVegRich, 
  "Shannon Div."        = cat_bm_shannon,
  "Native Shannon Div."  = cat_bm_natShannon
)


# 2. AUTOMATIC AIC EXTRACTION: Grab AICs and find the top models
# We calculate delta AIC (dAIC). Any model within 2 units of the absolute lowest AIC is a "top model"
aic_values <- sapply(bm_model_list, AIC)
min_aic <- min(aic_values)

aic_df <- data.frame(
  predictor = names(aic_values),
  aic = aic_values,
  daic = aic_values - min_aic,
  # Dynamically flag if a model is among the best (dAIC <= 2)
  is_best = (aic_values - min_aic) <= 2
)

# 3. Extract standardized parameters and force them into dataframes
standardized_list <- lapply(bm_model_list, function(mod) {
  as.data.frame(standardize_parameters(mod, method = "refit", ci = 0.95))
})

all_standardized <- bind_rows(standardized_list, .id = "Predictor")
names(all_standardized) <- tolower(names(all_standardized))

# 4. Exact lowercase terms matching your continuous model predictors
target_terms <- c(
  "totalveg", "prop_native", "olive", "mfr", "barberry", "blackberry", 
  "coralberry", "veg_rich", "native_veg_rich", "shannondiv", "native_shannondiv"
)

# 5. Filter, merge AIC flags, and build conditional formatting
plot_data <- all_standardized %>%
  filter(parameter %in% target_terms) %>%
  left_join(aic_df, by = "predictor") %>%
  mutate(
    # Keep ordering by effect size size, or change to '-aic' if you want top models at the top
    predictor = fct_reorder(predictor, std_coefficient),
    
    # STRATEGY 1: Add asterisks dynamically to the text labels of top models
    text_label = ifelse(is_best,
                        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f) *", std_coefficient, ci_low, ci_high),
                        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", std_coefficient, ci_low, ci_high)),
    
    # Create a nice group variable for ggplot coloring
    highlight_group = ifelse(is_best, "Top Model (dAIC ≤ 2)", "Other Model")
  )

# 6. Define axis boundaries for the standardized variables
x_lower_limit <- -1.5
x_upper_limit <- 1.5

# 7. Generate the final styled forest plot
bm_effects_plot <- 
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(y = predictor, color = highlight_group)) +
  # Baseline zero line (No effect)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Standardized confidence intervals
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high), height = 0.15, linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Standardized point estimates
  geom_point(aes(x = std_coefficient), size = 4) +
  
  # STRATEGY 2: Dynamic text table on the right margin 
  # We make the text bold if it is a top model to double down on formatting
  # geom_text(aes(x = x_upper_limit + 0.2, label = text_label, fontface = ifelse(is_best, "bold", "plain")), 
  #           hjust = 0, size = 3.5, color = "black") +
  
  # Set your specific custom colors (e.g., sharp dark red for top models, slate grey for others)
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top Model (dAIC ≤ 2)" = "firebrick3", "Other Model" = "lightsteelblue4")) +
  
  # Prevent extra-wide confidence intervals from ruining the visual layout
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(x_lower_limit, x_upper_limit), clip = "on") +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.2))) + # Reserves 45% empty space on the right
  labs(
    title = "Caterpillar Biomass",
    #subtitle = "Top performing AIC models highlighted in red with an asterisk (*)",
    x = "Standardized Coefficient (95% CI)",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Model Fit (AIC)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.box.background = element_rect(color = "black"),
    legend.position.inside = c(0.75, 0.25) # X and Y coordinates between 0 and 1
  )+
  geom_text(aes(x = -1.5, y = 11, label = "B"),
            colour="black")

bm_effects_plot

Fig4 <- grid.arrange(abund_effects_plot, bm_effects_plot, ncol = 1)
```
